supervised-fine-tuning.name: supervised fine-tuning
supervised-fine-tuning.definition: Continuing model training on labeled prompt-response demonstrations.
supervised-fine-tuning.explanation: Supervised fine-tuning presents desired responses after prompts and optimizes their next-token cross-entropy. It can update every model parameter or a selected subset. Falling training loss shows that optimization fits the demonstrations; held-out prompts are needed to measure transfer, and earlier tasks are needed to detect forgetting. The resulting behavior reflects the supplied examples, their formatting, coverage, hidden errors, and provenance.

lora.name: LoRA
lora.definition: A trainable low-rank update added to a frozen weight matrix.
lora.explanation: Low-Rank Adaptation writes an effective weight as a frozen base plus the product of two narrow matrices, usually scaled by alpha divided by rank. One factor is initialized to zero so the adapter initially preserves the base output, while the other is nonzero so gradients can begin. LoRA reduces trainable parameters and task-specific checkpoint size; useful rank and target modules depend on evaluation.

knowledge-distillation.name: knowledge distillation
knowledge-distillation.definition: Training a student model to match a teacher model’s output distribution.
knowledge-distillation.explanation: Distillation uses soft probabilities from a teacher as targets for a student, exposing relationships among alternatives that a single hard next-token target omits. The student may have a smaller architecture. Temperature can soften distributions, but the objective and derivative scaling must use that temperature consistently. A lower teacher-student divergence shows imitation on the transfer set, not factual correctness or broad equivalence.

checks: LoRA starts with exactly zero parameter change and lowers loss
Base parameter values remain unchanged after adapter training
One adapter gradient matches central differences
Soft-target gradient matches direct cross-entropy finite differences
Student KL to teacher falls and remains correct for a confidently wrong student
limitations: Base decoder is pretrained only on tiny synthetic cycles, not a useful language model
SFT and LoRA quality is measured only on tiny training fixtures
LoRA targets only the output projection
Distillation uses temperature tau=1 and V hard-target backward passes per example
Loss covers full sequences rather than masking prompt tokens
LoRA computes a full backward pass on a cloned effective model, so trainable parameter counts do not establish memory or speed savings
